correctness.rationale: For every three-one circular binary word with cyclic zero gaps (a,b,c), a rotation beginning at a marker has form 1 0^R 1 0^T 1 0^L; examining all proper border starts at either later marker shows it is unbordered iff L>R. A rotation beginning at the first zero after a marker is the reversal counterpart and is unbordered iff R>L; all other start positions share the same first/last zero and have a one-symbol border. Thus each unequal adjacent gap contributes exactly one unbordered rotation, and equal gaps contribute none. If gaps not all equal the word is primitive (its proper power exponent would be three, forcing equal gaps), hence U=1_{a!=b}+1_{b!=c}+1_{c!=a} is a count of DISTINCT conjugates, with possible values 0,2,3. For m zeros there are B=binom(m+2,2) ordered triples; all-equal δ=1_{3|m}, two-equal necklaces P-δ with P=floor(m/2)+1, and all-distinct (B-3P+2δ)/3. Orbit-size weighting yields E U=3(1-P/B) for uniform linear words. Independent direct border checks on every three-one linear word for m=0..15 confirmed necklace distribution and expected counts, including periodic case m=0; proof is for all m. The four-marker counterexample explicitly limits scope.
